scheme: keccak256(b"acr.decision::" + json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False, default=str))
warning: DO NOT REIMPLEMENT THIS IN ANOTHER LANGUAGE. Python renders a whole-valued float as 10.0 and JavaScript renders it as 10, and from JSON alone a reimplementation cannot tell which fields are floats. Call the Python helper, or ask ACR for the hash. These vectors exist to prove a mismatch loudly if anyone tries.

vectors.name: whole-valued floats
vectors.why: python emits 10.0, JSON.stringify emits 10 — the measured divergence

vectors.name: none is not absent
vectors.why: a null field is part of the record; dropping it is a different record

vectors.name: non-ascii is not escaped
vectors.why: ensure_ascii=False, so the bytes are UTF-8 and not \uXXXX

vectors.name: key order is sorted, not insertion
vectors.why: two dicts differing only in insertion order must hash the same

vectors.name: small decimals keep every place
vectors.why: 0.004410 is the real agent payment; trailing zeros are significant in the string

vectors.name: empty record
vectors.why: the degenerate case, so a reimplementation cannot special-case it away
